notes: Portable C++ and Java translation of the mapped native three-member timed-save resignation case. The native case title mentions FQR, but its body never calls flushQueueRequest; this contract covers resignation of a time-constrained member during a pending timed save, not FQR behavior. The adapter supplies provider, FOM, endpoint, callback model, and logical-time implementation. Under HLA_EVOKED, after one constrained member resigns, the surviving constrained member's TAR at save time 5 admits the save before its grant, the regulator initiates, and the surviving members complete the save without callbacks to the departed member. Six direct requirement-section pairs cover clauses 4.12, 4.19, 4.19.6, and 4.20. C++ primary and contract passed against an installed package under integer64 and float64 time using an adapter-supplied portable FOM. Java compiles against the official API only; provider runtime is unverified. This is experimental public-API evidence, not a universal cross-service ordering, FQR, immediate-callback, transport, interoperability, or conformance claim.
